mainTopic: Levels of purity in the משנה, hand-washing for חולין and מעשר, and intent in washing (חגיגה 18b)
overview: This משנה lays out a ladder of holiness: חולין, then מעשר, then תרומה, then קודש, then חטאת (the water of the red heifer). Each higher level demands more care about purity. First it shows how hands are purified for each level. Next it teaches that a טבילה counts only for the level a person had in mind. It then shows that clothes are treated as מדרס for anyone one level stricter, even the clothes of great people like יוסף בן יועזר and יוחנן בן גודגדא. The גמרא then asks whether חולין and מעשר really need hand-washing, since a משנה in ביכורים says they do not. It solves the מעשר clash by showing that רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about it. After רב שימי בר אשי rejects an eating-versus-touching answer, the גמרא settles the חולין clash: bread needs washing and fruit does not. Finally a ברייתא says washing hands needs intent, another ברייתא says it does not, and רב נחמן begins to resolve them. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How hands are purified for each level of holiness
steps.stepSummary: For חולין, מעשר and תרומה, pouring water on the hands is enough. For קודש the hands must be immersed. For חטאת, impure hands make the whole body impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One washes the hands by pouring water for חולין, מעשר and תרומה. For קודש, one immerses the hands. For חטאת, if his hands became impure, his whole body becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens by listing how hands are purified before handling food or items of different holiness levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The higher the level of holiness, the stronger the purification needed. Simple pouring (נטילת ידים) works for the three lower levels, but קודש needs a real dipping of the hands. For חטאת the חכמים were so strict that impure hands count as an impure body, so he must immerse fully.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing the hands by pouring water over them
One immerses (dips the hands into a מקוה)
Here: the water mixed with the ashes of the red heifer

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, חטאת does not mean a sin-offering. It means the special water of the red heifer, which is the highest level on this ladder.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One washes the hands (by pouring water)
for non-holy food, for tithe, and for teruma;
but for sacrificial food, one immerses (the hands).
And for the purification water, if his hands became impure,
his whole body becomes impure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouring water on the hands is enough for חולין, מעשר and תרומה. קודש requires immersing the hands. For חטאת, impure hands make the whole body impure.

steps.title: Immersion counts only for the level you intended
steps.stepSummary: A person who immersed with one level in mind is pure only for that level, not for the level above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he immersed for חולין and so is treated as pure for חולין, he may not eat מעשר. If he immersed for מעשר, he may not eat תרומה. If he immersed for תרומה, he may not eat קודש. If he immersed for קודש, he may not touch חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from hands to full-body טבילה and goes up the ladder one level at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What a person has in mind during טבילה sets the level of purity he reaches. He gets a חזקה (presumed status) of purity only for the level he intended. Each step up needs a new טבילה with the higher level in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: He is presumed to have a certain status (here: pure)

phrases.aramaic: טָבַל לַחוּלִּין, הוּחְזַק לַחוּלִּין — אָסוּר לַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: If he immersed for non-holy food, he is presumed pure for non-holy food, but is forbidden to eat tithe.

phrases.aramaic: טָבַל לַמַּעֲשֵׂר, הוּחְזַק לַמַּעֲשֵׂר — אָסוּר לַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: If he immersed for tithe, he is presumed pure for tithe, but is forbidden to eat teruma.

phrases.aramaic: טָבַל לַתְּרוּמָה, הוּחְזַק לַתְּרוּמָה — אָסוּר לַקּוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: If he immersed for teruma, he is presumed pure for teruma, but is forbidden to eat sacrificial food.

phrases.aramaic: טָבַל לַקּוֹדֶשׁ, הוּחְזַק לַקּוֹדֶשׁ — אָסוּר לַחַטָּאת.
phrases.english: If he immersed for sacrificial food, he is presumed pure for sacrificial food, but is forbidden to handle the purification water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same five-level ladder, now for full-body טבילה and intent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Purity from טבילה works only up to the level a person intended.

steps.title: Two general rules about immersion
steps.stepSummary: Immersing for a strict level covers the easier levels. Immersing without intending to become pure does not count at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he immersed for the strict level, he is allowed the easier levels. If he immersed but did not intend to become pure, it is as if he did not immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the list with two general rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule is the other side of step 2: purity works downward, so higher intent covers everything below it. The second rule shows that intent matters. A טבילה with no intent to become pure counts as if it never happened.
steps.whatToRemember: Intent during טבילה decides how far up the ladder it reaches. Purity works downward, never upward, and with no intent there is no purity at all.

phrases.english: If he immersed for the strict level, he is permitted for the lenient one.

phrases.aramaic: טָבַל וְלֹא הוּחְזַק — כְּאִילּוּ לֹא טָבַל.
phrases.english: If he immersed but did not intend to take on pure status, it is as if he did not immerse.
phrases.notes: Literally 'and was not presumed', meaning he went in without any intent to become pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the case-by-case list into general rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing for a higher level permits the lower levels. Immersing without intent to become pure is worthless.

steps.title: Clothing is impure for anyone one level higher
steps.stepSummary: The clothes of each group are treated as impure with מדרס for the group one level stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The clothes of an עם הארץ are מדרס for פרושין. The clothes of פרושין are מדרס for those who eat תרומה. The clothes of those who eat תרומה are מדרס for קודש. The clothes of those who eat קודש are מדרס for חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now applies the same ladder to clothing and shows how each group treats the clothes of the group below it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stricter group worries that a less careful person's clothes may have been sat or leaned on by a זב, which would make them מדרס, a strong level of impurity. So someone at a higher level treats the clothes of a lower-level person as מדרס. Even very careful people are 'not careful enough' for the level above them.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from a זב pressing (sitting, lying, leaning) on an item; it is a main source of impurity
A person not careful about purity laws
People careful to eat even ordinary food in purity

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody saw a זב touch these clothes. The rule treats them as מדרס for the higher group because the lower group was not careful at that higher level.

phrases.english: The clothes of an am ha'aretz are treated as midras for perushin.
The clothes of perushin are treated as midras for those who eat teruma.
The clothes of those who eat teruma are treated as midras for sacrificial food.
The clothes of those who eat sacrificial food are treated as midras for the purification water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same holiness ladder to clothing instead of to טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each group's clothes are treated as מדרס for the group one level stricter.

steps.title: Two very careful people who still fell one level short
steps.stepSummary: Even יוסף בן יועזר and יוחנן בן גודגדא, who were extremely careful, had cloths that counted as מדרס for the level above theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: יוסף בן יועזר was the most pious in the priesthood, yet his cloth was מדרס for קודש. יוחנן בן גודגדא ate his ordinary food with the purity of קודש all his life, yet his cloth was מדרס for חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with two real-life examples of the clothing rule from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף בן יועזר was careful at the level of תרומה, so his cloth was still מדרס for קודש. יוחנן בן גודגדא went further, to the level of קודש, yet his cloth was still מדרס for חטאת. No matter how holy a person is, the rule holds: being careful at one level does not cover the next level up.

keyTerms.meaning: The purity standard required for קודש

steps.whatToRemember: The ladder is חולין, מעשר, תרומה, קודש, חטאת. Purity reached at one level, whether through טבילה or through general care, never covers the level above it.
steps.whyThisMatters: These stories show the rule is not about a person's character. It is about the exact level of care he took on.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר הָיָה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: Yosef ben Yo'ezer was the most pious of the priesthood,
yet his cloth was treated as midras for sacrificial food.
Yochanan ben Gudgeda would eat (his food)
with the purity of sacrificial food all his days,
yet his cloth was treated as midras for the purification water.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר הָיָה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the clothing rule from step 4 applied even to great people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the most careful people's cloths were מדרס for the level above the one they kept.

steps.title: Do non-sacred food and tithe really need hand-washing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking whether חולין and מעשר really require נטילת ידים, as our משנה stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Do non-sacred food and tithe really need washing of the hands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with a basic question about our משנה. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said that pouring water on the hands is enough for חולין, מעשר and תרומה. That assumes that חולין and מעשר need hand-washing at all. The גמרא questions that assumption, and the next line shows why.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
Tithe (here, the second tithe eaten in ירושלים)
Washing the hands by pouring water on them

phrases.english: GEMARA: Non-sacred food and tithe,
do they require washing of the hands?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּלִּין וּמַעֲשֵׂר מִי בָּעוּ נְטִילַת יָדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the first rule of the משנה (step 1).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חולין and מעשר really require נטילת ידים, as our משנה implies.

steps.title: A משנה in ביכורים lists laws that apply to תרומה and ביכורים but not to מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that lists laws for תרומה and ביכורים, including נטילת ידים, and says these do not apply to מעשר, and all the more so not to חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: For תרומה and ביכורים one is liable to death and to adding a fifth. They are forbidden to non-כהנים, and they are the property of the כהן. They become nullified only in one hundred and one, and they require hand-washing and sunset. These laws apply to תרומה and ביכורים, but not to מעשר, and all the more so not to חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from ביכורים that seems to say מעשר and חולין do not need נטילת ידים. This quote sets up the contradiction that the גמרא will spell out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists several laws that apply only to holy foods like תרומה and ביכורים, and one of them is נטילת ידים. Then it says clearly that these laws do not apply to מעשר. If they don't even apply to מעשר, they certainly don't apply to חולין, which is less holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (one source against another)
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש and given to the כהן
An extra fifth added when paying back
Nullified in a mixture of one hundred and one

steps.confusionAlert: This quote comes from a different משנה, in ביכורים, not from our משנה. Our משנה said חולין and מעשר need hand-washing. This משנה seems to say they don't.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Terumah and first fruits:
one is liable for them to death and to a fifth,
phrases.notes: If someone ate them by mistake, he pays back what he ate plus an extra fifth.

phrases.english: and they are forbidden to non-priests,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and they are the property of the priest.
And they are nullified in one hundred and one,
and they require washing of the hands and sunset.
These apply to terumah and first fruits,
which is not so with tithe,
and all the more so with non-sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the question of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in our משנה (step 1) that חולין and מעשר require נטילת ידים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ביכורים משנה lists נטילת ידים as a law only for תרומה and ביכורים, and says it does not apply to מעשר or חולין.

steps.title: Two contradictions: about tithe and about non-sacred food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: our משנה and the ביכורים משנה disagree about מעשר, and they also disagree about חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between the two rulings about מעשר, and a contradiction between the two rulings about חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the contradiction clearly. There are two problems: one about מעשר and one about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says both מעשר and חולין need hand-washing. The ביכורים משנה says neither does. So each one conflicts separately, and each needs its own answer.

phrases.english: Tithe is difficult against tithe,
phrases.notes: He means the ruling about מעשר in one משנה contradicts the ruling about מעשר in the other.

phrases.english: non-sacred food is difficult against non-sacred food!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא מַעֲשֵׂר אַמַּעֲשֵׂר, קַשְׁיָא חוּלִּין אַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conflict raised by the source quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rulings on מעשר and חולין (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two משניות give opposite rulings on the same two foods, so there are two separate contradictions.

steps.title: The tithe contradiction is solved: the two משניות follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the מעשר contradiction: the ביכורים משנה follows רבי מאיר, and our משנה follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the contradiction about מעשר is not difficult: this משנה follows רבי מאיר, and that משנה follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the first problem, about מעשר, by saying the two משניות reflect two different opinions. The word בשלמא hints that the חולין problem is still unsolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes two משניות disagree because they were taught by רבנן who disagree with each other. Here the ביכורים משנה, which says מעשר needs no washing, is רבי מאיר's view. Our משנה, which requires washing for מעשר, follows רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this part is fine (hinting another part is still a problem)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: solving a contradiction by assigning each source to a different opinion. The חולין question is taken up in steps 11 through 14, where it is finally answered.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the מעשר contradiction is solved here. בשלמא means the חולין contradiction still needs an answer, which comes in steps 12 through 14.

phrases.english: Granted, tithe against tithe
is not difficult:
this is Rabbi Meir and that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the ביכורים משנה, which follows רבי מאיר. 'That' is our משנה, which follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the double contradiction in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different authorities (תנאי היא): each משנה follows a different opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to state one agreed law, so they appeared to clash about מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ביכורים משנה follows רבי מאיר and our משנה follows רבנן, so there is no contradiction about מעשר. The חולין contradiction remains.

steps.title: Source showing רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי מאיר says rabbinic-level impurity does not affect חולין or מעשר, while חכמים say it does affect מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: anything that needs immersion in water by rabbinic law makes holy food impure and disqualifies תרומה, but is allowed for חולין and מעשר. This is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים forbid it for מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove the answer from step 9, that רבי מאיר and רבנן really argue about מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, low-level rabbinic impurity does not touch מעשר at all, so no washing is needed for it, just as the ביכורים משנה says. חכמים are stricter about מעשר, which fits our משנה requiring washing for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in water, a purification step
By rabbinic law, not from the Torah
Disqualifies, without making it able to spread impurity further
And the Sages forbid, meaning they are stricter

phrases.english: As we learned: anything that requires immersion in water
by rabbinic law
makes sacred food impure,
and disqualifies תרומה,
and is permitted for חולין and for מעשר,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
But the Sages forbid it for מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for step 9's claim that the two משניות follow רבי מאיר and רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ביכורים משנה follows רבי מאיר and our משנה follows רבנן about מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פרה: רבי מאיר permits for חולין and מעשר; חכמים forbid for מעשר.

steps.title: The חולין contradiction is still unsolved
steps.stepSummary: The מעשר problem is solved, but the clash between the two משניות about חולין remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חולין against חולין is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer only fixed מעשר. The problem about חולין is still standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה just quoted, even חכמים only argue about מעשר, so everyone agrees חולין is not affected. That matches the ביכורים משנה but clashes with our משנה, which requires washing for חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of חולין in one source against the law of חולין in the other

phrases.english: But חולין against חולין is a difficulty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer from steps 9 and 10 covers only half of the problem raised in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that חולין requires נטילת ידים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No one, not even חכמים, treats חולין strictly, so the ruling in our משנה has no supporting view.

steps.title: First answer: eating versus touching
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה requires washing for eating חולין. The ביכורים משנה is only talking about touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is about eating, and there it is about touching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two משניות talk about different actions, eating and touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To eat חולין you must wash your hands, as our משנה says. To merely touch חולין you do not need to wash, which is what the ביכורים משנה means.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here it is about eating,
there it is about touching.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בַּאֲכִילָה, כָּאן בִּנְגִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חולין contradiction from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות talk about the same situation, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about eating; the other is about touching.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי rejects the eating/touching answer
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי argues that חכמים only disagree about eating מעשר. They agree that eating חולין needs no washing, so the first answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי objected: the Rabbis disagree with רבי מאיר only about eating מעשר. But about touching מעשר and eating חולין, do they not agree with him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי attacks the answer from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the פרה משנה we see that even חכמים are lenient about eating חולין. So nobody holds that eating חולין requires washing, and the eating/touching split cannot explain our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to this point (and no further)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi strongly objected to it:
The Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Meir
about eating מעשר,
but about touching מעשר
and eating חולין, don't they agree?
phrases.notes: He means: obviously they agree with רבי מאיר here, so eating חולין needs no washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that our משנה is about eating and the other is about touching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The disagreement is limited to eating מעשר, so all agree that eating חולין is lenient, and our משנה's rule is still unexplained.

steps.title: New answer: bread versus fruit
steps.stepSummary: Both משניות are about eating. Our משנה is about eating bread, which needs washing; the other is about eating fruit, which does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both are about eating. It is not difficult: here it is about eating bread, there about eating fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected answer with a new split: bread versus fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is no longer the action (eating or touching) but the food. Bread of חולין requires נטילת ידים; fruit of חולין does not, so the two משניות no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.english: Rather: both this and that are about eating,
and it is not difficult:
here it is about eating bread,
there it is about eating fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer after step 13 rejected the first one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is eating versus touching.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about eating; bread needs washing, fruit does not.
steps.whatToRemember: Final answer to the חולין contradiction: eating bread requires נטילת ידים, eating fruit does not.

steps.title: רב נחמן: washing for fruit is haughty
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's statement supports the idea that fruit does not need washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said: anyone who washes his hands for fruit is one of the haughty of spirit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the bread/fruit answer from רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If washing for fruit is considered showing off, then clearly there is no requirement to wash for fruit. That fits the claim that the ביכורים משנה is talking about fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Haughty people, who act more particular than needed

phrases.english: As Rav Naḥman said:
Anyone who washes his hands for fruit
is one of the haughty of spirit.

steps.raayaObject: The claim that fruit does not require נטילת ידים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן: washing for fruit is a sign of haughtiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: we do not wash hands before eating fruit.

steps.title: A ברייתא: washing hands needs intent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that washing or immersing hands purifies them only if the person intended to purify them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who washes his hands, if he intended, his hands are pure; if not, they are impure. The same for one who immerses his hands: with intent they are pure, without intent they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about whether you need intent when washing your hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says intent is required both for regular washing and for dipping hands in a מקוה. Without intent, the water does nothing, and the hands stay impure.

keyTerms.meaning: One who immerses (dips) in a מקוה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: one who washes his hands,
if he intended, his hands are pure,
if he did not intend, his hands are impure.
And likewise one who immerses his hands,
if he intended, his hands are pure,
if he did not intend, his hands are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about intent in washing hands, picking up the משנה's point that intent matters (step 3: טבל ולא הוחזק כאילו לא טבל).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing or immersing hands purifies only with intent.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says intent is not needed
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says hands are pure whether or not he intended.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: whether he intended or did not intend, his hands are pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a second one that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא needs intent and the second does not, so the two sources directly contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּין נִתְכַּוֵּון בֵּין לֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון —
phrases.english: But it was taught: whether he intended or did not intend,
his hands are pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּין נִתְכַּוֵּון בֵּין לֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that washing hands requires intent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says hands become pure even without intent.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins: one ברייתא is about חולין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן starts to resolve the contradiction by saying the lenient ברייתא is about חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: it is not difficult. Here it is for חולין,
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן begins his answer, splitting the two ברייתות by what kind of food the hands are washed for. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חולין, intent is not needed, so the ברייתא that says 'pure either way' is about חולין. The other side of the split, where intent is required, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: it is not difficult:
here it is for חולין,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the second ברייתא, which said intent is not needed. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the contradiction from step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות talk about the same kind of food, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is about חולין; the other half of the answer follows.
